concept: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits
summary: Source-anchored research for Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Validate fixture inputs as well as policies. Schema-aware request construction checks principal/action/resource/context compatibility; schema-based JSON parsing checks entity attributes and context shape. Cedar documents CLI and Rust Request::new() utilities, and cedarpy Entities.from_json_str accepts an optional schema. CLI 3.0.0 introduced request validation by default when a schema is supplied, with an explicit option to disable it. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k9securityio/cedar-py/main/README.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedar-policy/cedar/main/cedar-policy-cli/CHANGELOG.md

When the locally assumed schema changes, revalidate policies and rebuild or recheck request/entity fixtures. Cedar documents that previously valid policies can become invalid after a schema change; independently checking entity construction against the new schema helps expose fixture drift. (medium confidence)

Do not copy corpus-test leniency into a policy regression gate without review: cedar-py documents soft-passing policy/schema parse failures when a corpus fixture expects Deny. A stricter application gate should fail parse errors separately rather than treating them as successful negative tests. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Parsing and schema validation catch different defects: syntactically valid entity/action misspellings or invalid operand types can survive parsing. The independent cedar-py binding exposes PolicySet.from_str for parsing and validate_policies(policies, schema), returning validation_passed, for checking a supplied schema. These local checks do not establish Atlas compatibility. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k9securityio/cedar-py/main/README.md

An author-supplied schema lets local validation check declared entity types, actions, action-specific principal/resource types, context shapes, attribute names, and operator types. These checks test consistency with that supplied model. (medium confidence)

The upstream fixture harness separates `cedar validate --policies policies.cedar --schema schema.cedarschema --schema-format cedar` from `cedar authorize --policies policies.cedar --schema schema.cedarschema --schema-format cedar --entities entities.json --request-json request.json -v`; the two gates check different properties. (medium confidence)

Keep request JSON, entity data and expected outcomes together and rerun positive and negative cases after edits. The AWS sample Cedar test runner validates each policy file against a schema, then iterates ALLOW/*.json and DENY/*.json folders, invokes cedar authorize on each request JSON, and compares the actual decision with the folder name. AWS demonstrates a changed policy failing an expected-outcome test; cedarpy also exposes decision assertions and diagnostics. These are local scenario regressions, not Atlas conformance tests. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aws-samples/cedar-policy-validation-pipeline/main/policystore/tests/cedar_testrunner.sh ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/automate-cedar-policy-validation-with-aws-developer-tools/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k9securityio/cedar-py/main/README.md

For Atlas, local Cedar checks do not replace submitting policy bodies to Atlas's resource-policy validation endpoint or checking behavior in the non-production organization with a fresh cluster that MongoDB recommends. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/2025-02-19/operation/operation-validateorgresourcepolicies

A concrete implementation-parity counterexample was reported for cedar-go experimental strict validation: an October 17, 2026 reproduction on main b1be45e accepted undeclared enum entity IDs in policy scope that Rust cedar-policy 4.13.0 rejected. Record engine/build details with fixtures; this report is not evidence about Atlas and does not establish the current fix status. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-17)
